content: Clown and sharer; named first on the Greenwich court warrant
Plays Costard, Launce, Dogberry/Peter, and Bottom
He will stand on a hamper to be Alleyn, and the second roar costs him a glove.
He laughs loudest, and he pays for his own.
A sentence heard at second hand, about the Mayor and a player, is one he will keep.
An insult on paper delights him, and he would rather be the sorcerer than lose the phrase.
He can say a hard thing kindly and still refuse a quarrel.
He remembers the fortnight you were ill more accurately than the flour, and he would rather have the fear.
He can stay civil for a morning, and he does not want his name set beside a sum.
He still says you. He will grow a pass two lines at a time, and he will not name which lines were the better ones.
Thursday's additions were eleven lines, and he asks the interest on Burbage without being given a column for it.
He counts his own lines, he still says you, and he does not turn the count into a song.
He still says you, and he can put a whole grievance into a penny without asking for the Queen's twenty pounds.
On Wednesday, once his nine lines were in the book, he said he could no longer make up what he had made up, and he still wanted the credit for having made them up.
An empty sleeve does not buy him a new line, and he is still you.
He is still "you", and one crushed cake was the whole of the celebration he offered.
He will take a proverb when a coin is refused, and he is still addressed as you.
First on the paper, and first in the slippers. He takes the same share, and no extra.
He can be told the parts are not cast, and he can ask for a barrel, and he can walk out on his feet when both answers are no.
He took the jig on a thin Errors and was not told that the king has no fool in it.
He added nothing all week, had no jest on Saturday, and has not been told there is no fool in the king.
He will stop for the news at every door, arrive at the end, and ask where he comes in.
He will stay against a vote and still come to the ordinary.
He can play a napkin with no song in it, and he has no jest for the Guildhall.
He still says you, not thou. A king play with no fool in it, and he takes the jig as a groat in settlement of a pound.
He will say tour into a room that has already heard the word, and the room can leave it unagreed.
He stops eating when he hears sweet, and on the first night he tries Sweet Master Shakespeare once.
He had the name by heart in two days, and he pays a share out with a flourish.
He says the king wants a dog, and he says it to an apple.
He tells a share out with the name, and Sunday is the only day that interrupts him.
He has no line in the king and no interest on Garnish's tally, and he still thinks emptying a house is the rarer art.
They shout Remuneration at him, and he stays Sweet Master Shakespeare, and the bill is still the comedy.
Give him a pause and he will put a life in it, and he knows when not to claim the first place.
He took his hat off toward Bishopsgate and gave his thou to the mayor who was leaving.
He will take a short scene and he will not call the quarrel finished.
He is still on you, and a good night from him is not a new tally.
Thou begins at the sentence where he sees himself in the weaver, and not before.
He says thou. He will stop a joke that makes a workman a fool. Men first, and then the asses.
One line more than is set down is the whole of his luxury, and he knows what a false sum sounds like.
